title: Everyday Life and Ordinary New York
scope: Best-effort thematic research; verified card facts, editorial fit judgments; tokens are separate.

cards.name: Alicia Masters, Skilled Sculptor
cards.note: A working sculptor; an ordinary civilian gets a named role alongside the superheroes.

cards.name: Angry Rabble
cards.note: An angry crowd of city residents. Human Citizen is the actual type line.

cards.name: Aunt May
cards.note: A family member looking after the neighborhood; the Spider bonus does not make her a Spider creature.

cards.name: Bold Biochemist
cards.note: A scientist at work. Research is an ordinary profession even in a superhero setting.

cards.name: Cheering Crowd
cards.note: Spectators become the main event; the ability involves decisions by multiple players.

cards.name: Common Crook
cards.note: An everyday thief, explicitly a Human Rogue Villain; Villain does not necessarily mean superpowered.

cards.name: Crowd of True Believers
cards.note: Fans and spectators providing moral support.

cards.name: Daily Bugle Reporters
cards.note: Working journalists, with reporting-themed modes.

cards.name: Damage Control Crew
cards.note: The people who have to repair and clear up the city after everyone else's adventure.

cards.name: Doc Ock's Henchmen
cards.note: Hired muscle with a paycheck and a reluctance to fight Spider-Man.

cards.name: Everett K. Ross, Hapless Attaché
cards.note: A government liaison. His commander-specific ability still needs the chosen format to make sense.

cards.name: Flash Thompson, Spider-Fan
cards.note: This particular version is a civilian fan, distinct from Flash's powered identities.

cards.name: Foggy Nelson, On Retainer
cards.note: A lawyer: ideal for the legal-bills side of a city box.

cards.name: Gallant Citizen
cards.note: A helpful ordinary citizen, not a Hero by creature type.

cards.name: Guy in the Chair
cards.note: The friend providing technical support; the Spider-specific ability is a deck-building consideration.

cards.name: Happy Hogan, Bodyguard
cards.note: A bodyguard doing his job, with no superhuman identity on this card.

cards.name: Happy Hogan, Dauntless Driver
cards.note: A named driver; particularly appropriate for a transit or service-worker packet.

cards.name: J. Jonah Jameson
cards.note: The newspaper boss. Suspecting a pigeon is a possible game interaction, not a new house rule.

cards.name: Jarvis, Earth's Mightiest Butler
cards.note: A butler whose employers happen to be superheroes; his draw ability specifically needs Hero spells.

cards.name: Kingpin's Enforcers
cards.note: Organized crime's collection department: ordinary people with an unpleasant job.

cards.name: Mary Jane Watson
cards.note: A civilian performer; the card rewards Spiders but is itself Human Performer.

cards.name: Merciless Enforcers
cards.note: Street-level hired muscle, useful for ordinary-criminal themes.

cards.name: MJ, Rising Star
cards.note: The acting career rather than a superhero identity; a separate card from Mary Jane Watson.

cards.name: Mob Lookout
cards.note: Someone watching the street while a crime takes place.

cards.name: Oscorp Research Team
cards.note: Ordinary employees doing research for a spectacularly questionable company.

cards.name: Professional Wrestler
cards.note: A sports entertainer, with Performer and Warrior types rather than Citizen.

cards.name: Quinjet Technician
cards.note: An aircraft mechanic. The specialist mana ability supports power-up cards.

cards.name: Raft Security Officer
cards.note: A prison guard; the job is ordinary even though the inmates and equipment are not.

cards.name: Stark Industries Executive
cards.note: Corporate administration and financing, rather than a suit of superhero armor.

cards.name: Supportive Parents
cards.note: Parents helping their child: one of the clearest everyday-life cards.

cards.name: Taxi Driver
cards.note: Exactly the urban transport worker the theme wants.

cards.name: The Mary Janes
cards.note: A band. The members' other stories do not change this card's musical premise.

cards.name: Unlucky Witness
cards.note: Someone who saw the wrong thing at the wrong time.

cards.name: Willie Lumpkin, Postman
cards.note: Postal delivery continues even when the city is full of superheroes.

cards.name: Doctor Jane Foster
cards.note: The card presents a doctor, but Jane also has major supernatural identities in Marvel. A good civilian-role option if that distinction suits the box.

cards.name: Donald Blake, Guise of Thor
cards.note: Starts as a doctor but explicitly becomes a God Warrior Hero through its ability; not purely an ordinary person.

cards.name: Inner Demons Gangsters
cards.note: Street criminals with an explicitly supernatural affiliation. Useful if the gang aesthetic outweighs that connection.

cards.name: Armed Assailant
cards.note: Looks like an armed criminal, but the flavor identifies Melter and his villain technology. Do not assume a generic unpowered mugger.

cards.name: Glamorous Grapplers
cards.note: The professional-wrestling joke fits, but these are Marvel villain performers rather than a promise of ordinary athletes.

cards.name: Roxxon Brutes
cards.note: Corporate thugs are a strong city premise; their villain presentation and escalating strength make this a looser fit.

cards.name: TVA Bureaucrat
cards.note: Bureaucracy is mundane; administering timelines is not. A particularly good workplace joke.

cards.name: Rick Jones, Destined Sidekick
cards.note: A human sidekick on this card, with a much less ordinary wider Marvel history and explicit Hero support.

cards.name: Queen Mother Ramonda
cards.note: An unpowered human ruler, but royalty and Wakanda are a stretch from everyday New York. Introduces the monarch rules.

cards.name: City Pigeon
cards.note: The central city-wildlife joke. Bird, not Citizen; its departure creates a Food token.

cards.name: Lucky the Pizza Dog
cards.note: An ordinary named dog with an extremely suitable interest in food.

cards.name: Kraven's Cats
cards.note: Trained big cats associated with a villain. More zoo or escaped-animal material than normal street pets.

cards.name: Wakandan Tusker
cards.note: An elephant rather than a superhero; better as zoo or wildlife material than a New York native.

cards.name: Birds of Paradise
cards.note: Ordinary birds in a Marvel printing; wildlife rather than a pigeon on the subway. Inspect the particular art rather than inferring the species from the card name.

cards.name: Venomized Cat
cards.note: The owner's explicit near-match: an ordinary little cat acquired alien symbiote goo. Actual types include Symbiote and Villain.

cards.name: Masked Meower
cards.note: A neighborhood cat doing superhero work, with Spider Cat Hero types. Funny pet premise, genuinely powered.

cards.name: Radioactive Spider
cards.note: A small spider makes an excellent mundane-looking threat, but the radioactivity is the origin-story exception.

cards.name: Pet Avengers
cards.type_line: Creature — Dragon Cat Dog Bird Frog Hero
cards.note: A team of pets with heroic and fantastical members; not a collection of ordinary animals.

cards.name: Hit-Monkey
cards.note: The small-animal joke survives, but an armed assassin monkey is decidedly extraordinary.

cards.name: Bagel and Schmear
cards.note: Breakfast as a game piece; an actual Food artifact with two ways to use it.

cards.name: Hot Dog Cart
cards.note: Street food and a mana source in one ordinary piece of city equipment.

cards.name: Daily Bugle Newspaper
cards.note: A physical newspaper, distinct from the building and the reporters.

cards.name: Peter Parker's Camera
cards.note: Ordinary photography equipment with film counters, despite its famous owner's name.

cards.name: Pictures of Spider-Man
cards.note: Selling photographs to a newspaper is mundane even when the subject is a superhero.

cards.name: News Helicopter
cards.note: Local news transport. It is an artifact creature — Construct, not a Vehicle, and it creates a Citizen token.

cards.name: Passenger Ferry
cards.note: Ordinary public transportation; an actual Vehicle with crew 2.

cards.name: Subway Train
cards.note: The commute becomes a win condition. Vehicle with crew 2, not a creature card in the library.

cards.name: Steel Wrecking Ball
cards.note: A real demolition tool; the surrounding superhero action does not change the object's ordinary nature.

cards.name: Wedding Ring
cards.note: An everyday ceremonial object. Its gameplay involves copying the ring and linking players, so check the format.

cards.name: Costume Closet
cards.note: A closet is ordinary, but these are superhero outfits and the counter-moving machinery makes that association explicit.

cards.name: Iron Suitcase
cards.note: Looks like luggage; its ability turns it into a flying Construct. A very clear ordinary-object/extraordinary-secret joke.

cards.name: Captain America's Motorcycle
cards.note: A recognizable everyday vehicle, but specifically a superhero's customized equipment.

cards.name: The Thanos-Copter
cards.note: A helicopter with an absurdly overqualified owner. Deliberately not anonymous civilian transport.

cards.name: Spider-Mobile
cards.note: A car-shaped joke whose superhero equipment is part of the premise.

cards.name: Daily Bugle Building
cards.note: A newspaper office in the city; pairs naturally with its staff and paper.

cards.name: Fogwell's Gym
cards.note: An ordinary boxing gym with an especially good street-level identity.

cards.name: Hell's Kitchen
cards.note: A real New York neighborhood, represented as a land.

cards.name: University Campus
cards.note: Higher education and homework, with a city-appropriate setting.

cards.name: Urban Retreat
cards.note: Apartment hunting and somewhere to live; an excellent companion to Rent Is Due.

cards.name: Suburban Sanctuary
cards.note: A family home. More neighborhood/suburban than downtown, but clearly ordinary life.

cards.name: Vibrant Cityscape
cards.note: The city itself, without requiring a named superhero headquarters.

cards.name: Oscorp Industries
cards.note: An employer and office/laboratory complex, but tightly connected to superhero science and villains.

cards.name: Stark Industries
cards.note: Corporate life fits; the company's extraordinary technology is a visible thematic qualification.

cards.name: Fisk Tower
cards.note: Office-tower imagery with a very specific supervillain power structure behind it.

cards.name: Baxter Building
cards.note: A recognizable city building whose defining role is the Fantastic Four's extraordinary headquarters.

cards.name: Rent Is Due
cards.note: An enchantment about paying rent: one of the strongest everyday New York jokes.

cards.name: School Daze
cards.note: Exact spelling is Daze. An instant with Do Homework and Fight Crime modes; the homework premise qualifies, and both modes remain legal.

cards.name: Romantic Rendezvous
cards.note: Going on a date; no need to remove the card's normal draw/discard effect.

cards.name: Call Damage Control
cards.note: Calling the repair crew after something has gone wrong.

cards.name: Friendly Neighborhood
cards.note: An Aura that supplies ordinary Citizen tokens and a community-support ability.

cards.name: Parker Luck
cards.note: Bad luck and life refusing to go to plan. The particular unlucky resident happens to be Peter Parker.

cards.name: Scout the City
cards.note: Looking around town; its alternate removal mode does not erase that ordinary premise.

cards.name: Wisecrack
cards.note: Making a joke at someone's expense. Superhero context, ordinary human behavior.

cards.name: Political Triumph
cards.note: Politics as a city-life theme. It is an Enchantment — Plan, not an instant or sorcery.

cards.name: Heroes' Hangout
cards.note: Date Night is thoroughly ordinary; Patrol Night and the heroes in the title make the mixed premise explicit.

cards.name: Heroic Feast
cards.note: Dinner is ordinary, but the gathering and presentation explicitly center heroes.

cards.name: Prison Break
cards.note: A recognizable crime story, with a superhero-villain breakout in this printing.

cards.name: Secret Identity
cards.note: Conceal becomes an ordinary Citizen; Reveal explicitly produces a flying Hero. Keep both modes unless a box deliberately changes a rule.

cards.name: Risky Research
cards.note: Laboratory work fits, but the radiation and villain-science framing are the qualification.

cards.name: Action News Crew
cards.note: A local television news team from TMNT; strong crossover material for the Daily Bugle's competition.

cards.name: April O'Neil, Human Element
cards.note: A human investigator among mutants. A suitable ordinary-person crossover guest.

cards.name: April O'Neil, Live on the Scene
cards.note: Reporting from the scene of yet another extraordinary city incident.

cards.name: April, Reporter of the Weird
cards.note: A journalist doing her job; the things she reports on are the weird part.

cards.name: April O'Neil, Hacktivist
cards.note: A human using computers and investigation, with a contemporary technical-work theme.

cards.name: Courier of Comestibles
cards.note: A food-delivery worker, especially appropriate for a city lunch or takeout packet.

cards.name: Purple Dragon Punks
cards.note: Ordinary street-gang members from a New York crossover setting.

cards.name: Cat Collector
cards.note: A person with cats; the occupation/hobby is ordinary, while the printing's setting is Magic fantasy.

cards.name: Dog Walker
cards.note: Exactly the right urban job, presented in Ravnica's fantasy-city setting.

cards.name: Civic Gardener
cards.note: The city's landscaping staff; New Capenna's period city aesthetic rather than current New York.

cards.name: Cleanup Crew
cards.note: A work crew cleaning up the mess, in a fantasy-city setting.

cards.name: Corrupt Court Official
cards.note: Municipal corruption and paperwork. Choose the New Capenna printing for the city-crime aesthetic.

cards.name: Expendable Lackey
cards.note: A minor employee of a crime organization; a human in a fantasy city.

cards.name: Gathering Throng
cards.note: A crowd of ordinary people. Its same-name search ability specifically wants duplicates, so it may not suit a singleton box.

cards.name: Scheming Fence
cards.note: A dealer in stolen goods, with crime-city rather than superhero flavor.

cards.name: Sizzling Soloist
cards.note: A musician performing for a crowd; the New Capenna setting is the main qualification.

cards.name: Errant, Street Artist
cards.note: Street art and a contemporary-feeling occupation, within a fantasy city.

cards.name: Snooping Newsie
cards.note: A newspaper seller/informant with a particularly strong city-life identity.

cards.name: Tavern Swindler
cards.note: A bar-room con artist. Its coin-flip ability still needs a player to operate it.

cards.name: Night Clubber
cards.note: Nightlife in New Capenna; useful both as a literal club patron and a name joke.

cards.name: Professional Face-Breaker
cards.note: A paid brawler or enforcer; street-crime atmosphere, but an aggressive rather than peaceful everyday role.

cards.name: Caldaia Strongarm
cards.note: Crime-family muscle in a period-style city.

cards.name: Riveteers Decoy
cards.note: A worker/gang member used as a diversion; fantasy-city crime context.

cards.name: Wrecking Crew
cards.note: Demolition workers with a second life as hired muscle.

cards.name: Backup Agent
cards.note: A supporting operative in New Capenna; human, not a costumed superhero.

cards.name: Inside Source
cards.note: An informant in a city investigation, with an ordinary human role.

cards.name: Jaded Analyst
cards.note: The tired specialist looking through information; Ravnican detective setting.

cards.name: Case File Auditor
cards.note: Paperwork and administrative review as a creature card.

cards.name: Homicide Investigator
cards.note: A detective investigating an ordinary kind of crime in an extraordinary city.

cards.name: Novice Inspector
cards.note: An inexperienced investigator. Human Detective is the printed creature type.

cards.name: Projektor Inspector
cards.note: An investigator using Ravnican equipment; the profession fits more closely than the technology.

cards.name: Seasoned Consultant
cards.note: The experienced colleague brought in to help with a case.

cards.name: Person of Interest
cards.note: A suspect rather than a superhero, with a human type line.

cards.name: Pompous Gadabout
cards.note: An ordinary, irritating city resident; the joke is the personality.

cards.name: Sharp-Eyed Rookie
cards.note: A junior investigator in the fantasy-city police procedural pool.

cards.name: Meddling Youths
cards.note: Young amateur detectives; very suitable for a neighborhood-mystery packet.

cards.name: Delney, Streetwise Lookout
cards.note: A streetwise human lookout; named and mechanically strong, but not required for the theme.

cards.name: Dogged Detective
cards.note: An ordinary detective premise; choose an appropriate city printing.

cards.name: Detective of the Month
cards.note: Workplace recognition, with a detective doing the job.

cards.name: Serene Sleuth
cards.note: A calm investigator rather than a superhero identity.

cards.name: Sophia, Dogged Detective
cards.note: An investigator with a dog; particularly suitable for combining people and pets.

cards.name: Nelly Borca, Impulsive Accuser
cards.note: A named human investigator; a more theatrical city resident.

cards.name: Piper Wright, Publick Reporter
cards.note: A newspaper reporter from Fallout; the post-apocalyptic clothes and setting are the caveat.

cards.name: Three Dog, Galaxy News DJ
cards.note: A radio presenter from Fallout. Strong media-job fit, different world and visual era.

cards.name: Moira Brown, Guide Author
cards.note: A guidebook author and shopkeeper from a post-apocalyptic setting.

cards.name: Duchess, Wayward Tavernkeep
cards.note: Running a bar is ordinary; the Fallout setting is the departure.

cards.name: Sierra, Nuka's Biggest Fan
cards.note: An enthusiastic soda fan. Excellent mundane obsession, visibly a Fallout guest.

cards.name: Arcade Gannon
cards.note: A doctor from Fallout; a useful medical-worker candidate with a distinct franchise setting.

cards.name: Dr. Madison Li
cards.note: A scientist and engineer, with Fallout's technology and story attached.

cards.name: James, Wandering Dad // Follow Him
cards.type_line: Legendary Creature — Human Scientist // Instant — Adventure
cards.note: A father/scientist from Fallout; retain both the creature and Adventure rules.

cards.name: Barbara Wright
cards.note: A human teacher from Doctor Who; sci-fi context rather than innate superpowers.

cards.name: Ian Chesterton
cards.note: A human science teacher in an adventure setting.

cards.name: Martha Jones
cards.note: A human doctor from Doctor Who; the card's actual type is Human Cleric.

cards.name: Rory Williams
cards.note: A nurse as a character premise, but this Doctor Who version carries extraordinary story and time-related mechanics.

cards.name: Donna Noble
cards.note: An ordinary-worker personality with substantial extraordinary story context; not an unqualified mundane-character entry.

cards.name: Wilfred Mott
cards.note: An ordinary human relative and veteran from Doctor Who; a good older-resident guest.

cards.name: Dan Lewis
cards.note: An ordinary human companion from Doctor Who; a useful civilian rather than superhero guest.

cards.name: Graham O'Brien
cards.note: A human companion and bus-driver character; the card itself belongs to the Doctor Who setting.

cards.name: Yasmin Khan
cards.note: A human police officer from Doctor Who, printed as a Human Detective.

cards.name: Sarah Jane Smith
cards.note: A human investigative journalist; sci-fi adventures provide the setting caveat.

cards.name: Sally Sparrow
cards.note: A human investigating strange events; photographic and detective associations fit the city premise.

cards.name: Duggan, Private Detective
cards.note: A private detective from Doctor Who; especially suitable for a street-level investigation joke.

cards.name: Casey Jones, Vigilante
cards.note: An unpowered person with sports equipment, but deliberately acting as a vigilante rather than simply being a civilian.

cards.name: Casey Jones, Jury-Rig Justiciar
cards.note: Improvised equipment and an ordinary human underneath; the superhero-adjacent vigilante role is explicit.

cards.name: Casey Jones, Back Alley Brute
cards.note: A street-level brawler who is still a named action hero/vigilante.

cards.name: Casey Jones, Asphalt Hooligan
cards.note: City streets and sports equipment fit; masked vigilante behavior is the exception.

cards.name: Dockside Chef
cards.note: Cooking is mundane, but this is an enchantment creature in Kamigawa's supernatural setting, with sacrifice-based gameplay.

cards.name: Innocent Bystander
cards.note: A perfect ordinary-person role, but the person is a Goblin rather than a mundane human.

cards.name: Civil Servant
cards.note: A wonderfully ordinary job performed by an anthropomorphic Cat Citizen.

cards.name: Speakeasy Server
cards.note: Serving drinks is mundane; the server is a Bird Citizen.

cards.name: First Responder
cards.note: The emergency-service role is ideal, but this worker is an Ogre Citizen.

cards.name: Boss's Chauffeur
cards.note: An ordinary driving job, with an Elf Citizen doing it.

cards.name: Gary Clone
cards.note: An ordinary-looking human whose entire joke is being one of many clones. Also a poor reason by itself to require duplicate cards.

cards.name: Sanctuary Cat
cards.note: An ordinary small domestic cat; one of the closest non-Marvel answers to just a cat.

cards.name: Helpful Hunter
cards.note: A house-cat-scale hunter. Strong pet and pest-control material.

cards.name: Generous Stray
cards.note: A stray cat in a city setting; especially good for an alley-cat packet.

cards.name: Charmed Stray
cards.note: A small stray cat. Its same-name synergy is optional, not a reason the box must abandon singleton preferences.

cards.name: Garrison Cat
cards.note: A cat in a garrison rather than a modern apartment; the animal itself is ordinary-looking.

cards.name: Warehouse Tabby
cards.note: A warehouse cat: an exceptionally close fit for ordinary city animals.

cards.name: Forum Familiar
cards.note: A cat in a city environment, with disguise rules and a fantasy setting.

cards.name: Burglar Rat
cards.note: A city rat stealing something. The humorous job-like name does not make it a humanoid Citizen.

cards.name: Drainpipe Vermin
cards.note: A rat in urban plumbing: very strong sewer and street-life material.

cards.name: Sewer Rats
cards.note: Exactly the city pest the name suggests.

cards.name: Gnawing Vermin
cards.note: Ordinary pest behavior; particularly fitting around food and refuse.

cards.name: Innocuous Rat
cards.note: A deliberately unimpressive small rat, despite the surrounding horror set.

cards.name: Tunnel Rats
cards.note: Rats in the TMNT underground-city setting, rather than mutant humanoid turtles.

cards.name: Ravenous Rats
cards.set_name: Duel Decks Anthology: Garruk vs. Liliana
cards.note: Hungry rats with an ordinary-animal premise; select the printing whose art best suits the city.

cards.name: Swarm of Rats
cards.note: A group of rats; numbers matter mechanically without requiring identical non-token cards.

cards.name: Pack Rat
cards.note: A rat infestation with a token-copy engine; a balance consideration even in an ordinary-animal box.

cards.name: Rat Colony
cards.note: An infestation. Its special deck-construction permission allows duplicates but does not require using them.

cards.name: Relentless Rats
cards.note: The relentless pest joke fits, but the card's design strongly encourages multiple copies; optional for this project.

cards.name: Typhoid Rats
cards.note: A disease-carrying pest; ordinary danger rather than a superhero.

cards.name: Plague Rats
cards.note: An older infestation card that explicitly scales with other cards named Plague Rats.

cards.name: Pestilence Rats
cards.note: Rats as disease carriers; a darker version of the ordinary pest theme.

cards.name: Muck Rats
cards.note: Ordinary rats in a dirtier or more rural scene.

cards.name: Bog Rats
cards.note: Rats with a swamp setting rather than an urban one.

cards.name: Rabid Rats
cards.note: A real-world animal danger, though more unpleasant than a pet-comedy theme.

cards.name: Ruin Rat
cards.note: A scavenging rat in ancient ruins rather than a present-day subway.

cards.name: Tangled Colony
cards.note: An infestation in a fairy-tale setting; no need to treat it as a modern city by default.

cards.name: Voracious Vermin
cards.note: A hungry rat and its infestation support, in a fantasy setting.

cards.name: Thriving Rats
cards.note: Rats in Kaladesh's industrial world; plausible machine-room or factory pests.

cards.name: Undercity Dire Rat
cards.note: A rat in an urban underworld, but exaggerated Final Fantasy monster scale is the qualification.

cards.name: Carrier Pigeons
cards.note: Ordinary working pigeons. Excellent alongside City Pigeon and a newspaper or mail theme.

cards.name: Storm Crow
cards.note: A normal crow as a hilariously unimpressive threat; famous outside this project's joke as well.

cards.name: Murder of Crows
cards.note: A flock of ordinary-looking crows with a useful city-wildlife identity.

cards.name: Thieving Magpie
cards.note: A bird stealing shiny objects; suitable for parks, streets, and rooftops.

cards.name: Suntail Hawk
cards.note: A small hawk; believable city or park wildlife, with fantasy-setting art to check.

cards.name: Healer's Hawk
cards.note: A hawk in a city setting; lifelink is game text, not proof that the animal is a superhero.

cards.name: Rustwing Falcon
cards.note: A plausible urban raptor; period/fantasy art is the main qualification.

cards.name: War Falcon
cards.note: A trained falcon with a soldiers/knights restriction that may be awkward in a civilian box.

cards.name: Squadron Hawk
cards.note: Ordinary-looking hawks, but the same-name search ability specifically favors duplicates.

cards.name: Courier Hawk
cards.note: A bird carrying messages; thematically useful for mail without pretending it is a Human Citizen.

cards.name: Messenger Jays
cards.note: Birds carrying messages in a fantasy setting.

cards.name: Palace Familiar
cards.note: A small bird kept around a palace; fantasy context, ordinary-animal silhouette.

cards.name: Owl Familiar
cards.note: An owl with a familiar role; more magical association than an anonymous park owl.

cards.name: Sage Owl
cards.note: An owl, though the wisdom/scrying presentation is a fantasy association.

cards.name: Kingfisher
cards.note: An ordinary waterside bird; good for parks or waterfronts rather than apartments.

cards.name: Sea Eagle
cards.note: An ordinary coastal bird, suitable for the harbor side of the city.

cards.name: Welkin Tern
cards.set_name: Global Series Jiang Yanggu & Mu Yanling
cards.note: A seabird that can fit the waterfront, with fantasy-era artwork.

cards.name: Vexing Gull
cards.note: A gull: an excellent annoying urban-waterfront animal, despite its original setting.

cards.name: Nephalia Seakite
cards.note: A coastal bird with a fantasy place name.

cards.name: River Hoopoe
cards.note: An ordinary bird from a less urban environment.

cards.name: Coveted Peacock
cards.note: An ornamental park or zoo bird; a plausible city animal in a deliberately extravagant setting.

cards.name: Osai Vultures
cards.note: Ordinary scavengers, better for wildlife/zoo or outskirts than a normal city sidewalk.

cards.name: Circling Vultures
cards.note: Ordinary scavenging birds; the scene is less urban.

cards.name: Gorging Vulture
cards.note: A scavenging animal; a darker wildlife option.

cards.name: Selfless Savior
cards.note: An ordinary dog protecting someone. A strong pet candidate.

cards.name: Trusty Retriever
cards.note: A dog fetching something; very close to mundane pet behavior.

cards.name: Mischievous Pup
cards.note: A small dog causing trouble; fits the theme without needing a superhero identity.

cards.name: Alpine Watchdog
cards.note: A normal dog, with a mountain rather than city setting.

cards.name: Resolute Watchdog
cards.note: A guard dog in a city setting.

cards.name: Boros Mastiff
cards.note: A guard dog affiliated with a fantasy-city guild.

cards.name: Akroan Mastiff
cards.note: A mastiff with an ancient-world guard-dog role.

cards.name: Affa Guard Hound
cards.note: A guard dog in a fantasy settlement.

cards.name: Cathar's Companion
cards.note: An ordinary canine companion, but with a Gothic-fantasy owner and setting.

cards.name: Faithful Watchdog
cards.note: A watchdog; the selected printing's equipment and surroundings determine how contemporary it feels.

cards.name: Karlov Watchdog
cards.note: A dog belonging to a fantasy-city household.

cards.name: Rambunctious Mutt
cards.note: An enthusiastic ordinary mutt, suitable for a chaotic pet packet.

cards.name: Pack Mastiff
cards.note: A mastiff whose pump ability affects other Pack Mastiffs; note the same-name incentive before choosing duplicates.

cards.name: Pack Leader
cards.note: An ordinary-looking dog leading other dogs; tune its protective effect for the box.

cards.name: Loyal Warhound
cards.note: A trained dog with a military/fantasy setting rather than an apartment pet.

cards.name: Isamaru, Hound of Konda
cards.note: A named ordinary dog in an older Japanese-inspired fantasy setting.

cards.name: Yoshimaru, Ever Faithful
cards.note: A named dog; legendary-matters gameplay and partner are separate from its mundane appearance.

cards.name: Dogmeat, Ever Loyal
cards.note: An ordinary dog from Fallout; the post-apocalyptic equipment and scenery are the caveat.

cards.name: Guard Dogs
cards.note: Ordinary trained dogs with a period setting.

cards.name: Patrol Hound
cards.note: A working dog in a fantasy-world patrol.

cards.name: Wild Dogs
cards.note: Ordinary feral dogs rather than pets; check the control-changing text before using it in an automated deck.

cards.name: Mad Dog
cards.note: An aggressive ordinary dog; fits the joke at a rougher edge.

cards.name: Scrapyard Mongrel
cards.note: A dog among industrial scrap, with artifact synergy that suits a city junkyard.

cards.name: Thraben Purebloods
cards.note: Dogs in a Gothic-fantasy town, not supernatural dogs by creature type.

cards.name: Rin and Seri, Inseparable
cards.note: A cat-and-dog pair as a named creature. A strong pet premise with tribal support attached.

cards.name: Cheeky House-Mouse // Squeak By
